description: DEMO CONFIG. Every block below is annotated so the repo doubles as documentation.
config:recommended    - Renovate's maintained baseline preset. Dependabot has no preset system at all.
:dependencyDashboard  - opens ONE tracking issue listing every pending/rate-limited/errored update,
with checkboxes that create the PR on demand. Dependabot has no equivalent.
group:monorepos       - auto-groups packages published from the same monorepo (e.g. @typescript-eslint/*)
from a community-maintained list. Zero per-package config.
Security updates are grouped, but split by update type via a Handlebars template.
One combined PR would mix breaking majors (flask 3, urllib3 2, werkzeug 3) with safe
patches, go permanently red, and block every other CVE fix behind it. Two groups is
the smallest count that keeps the safe fixes mergeable.
Weekly PR that regenerates package-lock.json from scratch, refreshing TRANSITIVE
dependencies that no manifest change would ever touch. Dependabot has no counterpart:
it only bumps transitives when an advisory names them.

customManagers.description: Update `ARG <TOOL>_VERSION=` lines in the Dockerfile using inline `# renovate:` annotations. No built-in manager - and no Dependabot feature - can do this.

packageRules.description: LANE 1 - everything non-major, one PR. Collapsed across npm/gomod/pip/docker/actions/regex: acceptable because one team owns this repo. Split by language again if ownership is split.
LANE 2 - npm devDependencies stay in their own PR because this one automerges and nobody reads it. Overrides Lane 1 for devDeps.
LANE 3 - baseline for every major: isolated, soaked 21 days, held behind a dashboard checkbox.
LANE 4 - ESCALATION. Once the version actually in use is over 3 months old the checkbox gate lifts by itself, so nothing rots in the queue unnoticed. Still reviewed, never automerged.

LANE 4b - infra majors (Docker base image, GitHub Actions, regex-managed tool versions) collapse into ONE PR instead of one per action. Low blast radius and fully CI-verified, so grouping them is safe. Still inherits the approval gate from Lane 3 unless Lane 4 has escalated them.

LANE 5 - npm devDependency majors, grouped into ONE PR and automerged after a 30-day soak. Grouping majors is normally wrong; it is defensible here only because CI runs lint AND typecheck against them, so a breaking eslint or typescript major fails the build. Runtime deps are excluded: jsonwebtoken 8 to 9 typechecks clean and still changes signature-verification defaults at runtime.
prPriority only - runtime-critical packages surface first when the concurrent limit bites.
